text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: auth-service login failures detected against Okta JWKS — paging oncall

maria: seeing spikes of 401s from the auth proxy, starting ~10:34 UTC. Affected: login, console access, token introspect. Alerts: auth.errors.rate and frontend.login.failures.

maria: logs show 'jwt: key not found for kid' and 'token verification failed' across multiple services. Samples: `k8s/auth-proxy - 2026-07-12T10:35:02Z ERROR jwt: key not found for kid: xyz`

devon: I'm oncall for infra, joining. Any change in JWKS URL or config pushed recently?

sam: No recent deploys to auth-service from us, config hasn't changed. Okta status page shows a 'Partial Degradation' event in token validation region. Link: https://status.okta.example/incident/abc123 (internal link cached)

support-lin: customer reports: "Users can't sign in to the console" from two large enterprise tenants. CS is warming customers. Early estimate: ~4% of active sessions impacted, mostly interactive logins.

maria: Mitigation plan ideas: 1) enable cached JWKS fallback (we have code path to accept previously cached keys for 15m) 2) allow admin IPs with bypass cookie (short lived) 3) roll to token-accept variant that disables kid check and uses shared secret (risky).

oncall-frontend: Can we enable JWKS cache fallback now? That should re-enable most tokens if keys haven't rotated.

devon: I'll flip the flag on auth-configmap to enable jwks_cache_fallback=true and restart 2 pods at a time. Doing a canary first.

infra-bot: Deployment triggered by devon: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-service -n prod --selector=canary=true`

maria: Canary shows successful logins after fallback enabled. 200->302 for /oauth/authorize. Still seeing intermittent 401s for token introspect.

sam: Pushing a config to increase JWKS cache TTL from 60s -> 900s as a temporary measure.

devon: Config applied across prod. Rolling restarts continuing.

support-lin: CS update sent: "We're seeing degraded login for some customers; we've applied a temporary mitigation and are working with Okta." Customers asking for ETA.

maria: Next steps: 1) contact Okta support (we already have an open ticket) 2) monitor error rate and affected tenants 3) consider circuit-breaker for introspect failing downstreams to avoid cascading 500s.

sam: Okta replied: investigating JWKS propagation issue in their token service, no ETA yet. They advised use cached keys if possible.

support-lin: Adding list of affected tenants to shared doc: https://docs.internal/incident/1795023456/affected-tenants

devon: Rolling restarts done. Auth-service error rate dropped ~78% over last 12 minutes. Login success rate for console jumped from 86% -> 97% for canary cluster.

maria: Pushing a small change to auth-proxy to short-circuit introspect failures and return 503 to frontend to avoid bad UX loops. Deploying as emergency patch.

infra-bot: Patch deployment: `kubectl apply -f emergency/auth-introspect-shortcircuit.yaml` — rollout successful in 3 zones.

oncall-frontend: Frontend team: please implement client-side retry/backoff for 503 from /introspect for the next 24h. This will reduce failed login noise for users behind flaky introspect calls.

support-lin: Customer impact update: 6 enterprise customers reported console login failures, all notified with instructions and ETA TBD. No data loss.

sam: Metrics links: Auth errors dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/abc/auth-errors?orgId=1, Frontend login funnel: https://grafana.internal/d/xyz/login-funnel

maria: Root cause preliminary: Okta JWKS endpoint returned stale/partial keyset due to upstream propagation bug, causing our kid lookup to fail. Our mitigation using cached JWKS and extended TTL reduced impact.

devon: Post-incident manual actions: 1) add better JWKS caching fallback with longer TTL and verification warnings 2) add automated switch to cached keys when kid not found (with alert) 3) runbook update for Okta partial degradations.

support-lin: CS will follow up with impacted customers with timelines and compensation guidance if SLA thresholds hit.

maria: Moving to incident review phase. Need oncall handoff: devon you stay till 16:00 UTC, sam join for follow-up tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

devon: Acknowledged, will own the postmortem notes and timeline.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to P2. Pages cleared. If anything new crops up, reopen thread or create new incident.

support-lin: Thx everyone. Final note: Okta confirmed fix propagated at 11:02 UTC. We'll keep JWKS fallback for 2 hours before reverting.

maria: Logging final numbers: peak affected requests ~4200/min, total impacted sessions ~27k unique users during window, estimated customer-visible error rate peaked at 13% for interactive logins.

devon: I'll open the postmortem and link to this thread: https://docs.internal/postmortems/1795023456-auth-jwks-propagation.json

sam: Good job, quick mitigation. Let's follow up with the runbook edits and an alert that includes Okta status page cross-check.

support-lin: Closing customer comms loop now. Will post final update in two hours once rollback of fallback is confirmed. :white_check_mark:
